items.statement: A data, data1, or data2 hash points to a specific script binary hash.
A type hash finds code through a cell with a matching Type Script.
The lock authorizes spending the code cell; its Type Script validates replacement outputs.
The app can look up current cells, but it does not monitor changes or send alerts in the background.

faq.title: What the preview does and does not tell you

card.title: Read the CKB rules
card.text: Check the official explanation of data hashes, type hashes, and script upgrades.

items.q: Does a type hash prove that someone can upgrade the script?
items.a: It means the code hash is resolved through a matching Type Script cell. The lock authorizes spending, while the Type Script constrains replacement outputs. The checker shows both on-chain scripts but cannot infer a real-world controller from unfamiliar lock logic.

items.q: Can this page check any token or dApp?
items.a: It can scan a CKB address or analyze Script JSON. The MVP searches Type ID cells, reports current capacity and scripts, and traces up to 25 cell versions. It does not calculate token balances or interpret arbitrary lock code.

items.q: Are the examples real deployed contracts?
items.a: The Type reference example uses JoyID's published mainnet code hash and queries the selected chain. The data reference sample is illustrative and has no matching live binary lookup.

items.q: Does saving a script monitor it or send alerts?
items.a: No. Saving stores the Script and network in this browser. You can manually run the analysis again; background monitoring and notifications are not implemented.

items.q: Is my pasted script sent to a server?
items.a: The Script or address is sent to this app's API for a read-only query through the selected public CKB provider. Saved watchlist entries remain in this browser's local storage. Do not paste secrets.

items.q: Does a replaceable code reference mean my funds are unsafe?
items.a: Not by itself. The reference type does not tell you what the code does, who controls its lock, or whether a change would affect your particular asset. Inspect the evidence before drawing a conclusion.
